newsitem.title: USA: Kodak alleges former workers sold secrets.
newsitem.headline: Kodak alleges former workers sold secrets.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co said Friday it had filed suit alleging that former employees, including a supervisor and a developmental engineer, were involved in stealing and selling company secrets.
The suit names Harold Worden, formerly a supervisor at Kodak Park, the company's main film manufacturing center and its research and development headquarters, said Kodak spokesman James Blamphin.
Also named was Kurt Strobl, an engineer who left the company on Wednesday, Blamphin said.
Blamphin said the suit was filed after a year-long probe by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. He said the probe was begun at the request of the company.
Blamphin said Kodak believes the value of the information stolen and sold to potential competitors runs into the "tens of millions" of dollars.
He said the buyers came from "around the world."
In a letter to company employees released on Friday, Kodak said Worden retired in 1992 and set up a consulting firm, Worden Enterprises Inc.

It said Worden distributed material indicating that he had recruited about 60 former Kodak employees and had marketed these employees when providing technical and engineering services to clients that included Kodak competitors.
Blamphin said Worden was a technical associate in a supervisory position and Strobl was a senior engineer.
He said Worden worked on the "401 machine," a four-story-high, 60-foot-long machine makes clear plastic sheets that are coated with liquid emulsions to make film.
He said trade secrets that were stolen and marketed are detailed in a 48-page civil suit filed in Federal District Court in Rochester.
